investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state and the eval runner never reached the point of recording results.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) never returned vmIdPresent or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be absent and the contract to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs are holding all available slots, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.
[Likely] A peer-pod VM from a previous eval run was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may have failed silently), leaving a slot occupied and reducing available capacity to zero.

[Possible] The 4 nodes that do not match the pod's node affinity/selector have been cordoned, drained, tainted, or had their labels changed, reducing the schedulable node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, making exhaustion more likely.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node was reduced (e.g., via a node configuration or cloud quota change), shrinking total cluster capacity without a corresponding reduction in concurrent agent demand.

[Lower likelihood] A cluster autoscaler that would normally add peer-pod-capable nodes is not triggering, is misconfigured, or has hit a cloud quota ceiling, preventing horizontal expansion to relieve the pressure.

Because no pod could be scheduled, no agent was ever created, and the remote-agent-state probe never produced the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a full contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the two eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free resources, every remote-agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This prevents agent creation from completing, which in turn prevents the remote-agent-state probe from reaching the state-polling phase and producing any evidence. The failure is localized to the Kubernetes scheduling layer for the remote-agents swarm pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-19 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to time out and fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the only nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector targets only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are resource-saturated. If the affinity was recently tightened or node labels changed, the schedulable pool may have shrunk unexpectedly.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have enough VM slots to handle concurrent eval runs plus production workloads simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
Lower probability — leaked or zombie remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, reducing available capacity for new scheduling attempts.
